status.main_product: Milk and dairy products
status.scope_reason: The company operates as a core player because it produces lactoferrin ingredients commercially through its German subsidiary MILEI GmbH and supplies lactoferrin-infused commercial products under its own name.
status.evidence: According to the official Morinaga Milk Industry website, its German subsidiary MILEI GmbH produces lactoferrin and is a leading global large-scale production hub for the ingredient [.

claims.claim: A company-authored scientific publication outlines that global standardization regulations like EU Novel Food and US GRAS require more than 95% lactoferrin purity in protein, which means participating established producers like its subsidiary MILEI GmbH can supply high-grade lactoferrin exceeding this 95% threshold.
The company reports an investment of EUR 15,000,000 in its wholly owned German subsidiary, MILEI GmbH, to double its annual lactoferrin production capacity.

The company reports that this expansion project at the Leutkirch, Germany facility was planned to launch operations in April 2021, bringing its annual lactoferrin production capacity to approximately 170 tons.

The company reports developing a unique commercial chromatographic process using a weakly acidic cation exchange resin to extract and purify high-purity bovine lactoferrin from skim milk or whey, which was implemented on a large scale starting in 1989 through its German manufacturing subsidiary, MILEI GmbH.

The company reports employing carefully controlled pasteurisation and industrial milk processing technologies in combination with non-denaturing heat sterilization to extract and isolate bioactively intact lactoferrin.

claims.parameter: R&D and Clinical Evidence for Lactoferrin
claims.claim: Morinaga Milk Industry Co., Ltd. completed a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial demonstrating that 200 mg daily oral supplementation of bovine lactoferrin for 12 weeks supports immune health by improving winter respiratory and systemic symptoms through the activity of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs).

claims.parameter: R&D and Clinical Evidence for Lactoferrin
claims.claim: In a preliminary, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial completed in collaboration with Shinshu University, the company demonstrated that lactoferrin-supplemented formula improves sleep quality in children aged 12–32 months.

The company reports that its German subsidiary, MILEI GmbH, produces lactoferrin and posted a significant increase in revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, though specific financial figures or growth percentages for lactoferrin sales alone were not itemized.
claims.note: The significant increase in revenue for MILEI GmbH specifically for the full fiscal year ended March 2026 is unconfirmed in available financial reports.

claims.claim: The company reports that its wholly owned German subsidiary, MILEI GmbH, produces and supplies lactoferrin to global infant formula and supplement manufacturers, and positions the ingredient across its own B2B ingredient portfolio and approximately 30 internal branded products, such as its "Hagukumi" and "E-AKACHAN" infant formulas.
claims.note: The specific detail regarding lactoferrin being used across 'approximately 30 internal branded products' is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Morinaga Milk Industry Co., Ltd. secured US FDA Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) status for its cow's milk-derived lactoferrin in 2014, listed under GRN No. 464 for general food use (such as yogurt, powdered milk, and frozen desserts) and GRN No. 465 for use in term infant formulas.

The company obtained regulatory authorization from the European Commission in November 2012 (Commission Implementing Decision 2012/725/EU) approving its bovine lactoferrin as a novel food ingredient for the European Union market.

Morinaga Milk Industry Co., Ltd. is a publicly traded entity listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market, operating a vertically integrated dairy business that explicitly features lactoferrin within its functional and food ingredients segment.

The company manages its international production and supply of B2B lactoferrin for infant formula and nutritional food products through its wholly owned German subsidiary, MILEI GmbH, which was originally established as a joint venture in 1972 and later fully acquired in 2012.

The company reports an investment of EUR 15 million (approximately JPY 1.8 billion) allocated to its subsidiary MILEI GmbH to double its lactoferrin production capacity to approximately 170 tons per year, an operation that was scheduled to launch in April 2021.
